## Close record — merged as `6fb4d801c9` (change 1998, patchset 2)

Verified byte-identical before closing: all seven files in the merged commit carry the same
blob SHAs as my local commit, and the merged commit carries `Change-Id: Iaa42fa1c…`,
`rebar-ticket: 1241-b83c-f8c7-40bf` and the DCO sign-off.

### Acceptance criteria — one nuance, recorded rather than reworded

All four are ticked. AC4 says *"Reuse `tests/_child_diag.py` (`child_failure_detail` /
`assert_child_ran_clean`)"*. I reused **`child_failure_detail`** but deliberately did **not**
use `assert_child_ran_clean`: it demands a specific exit code (default `0`) and also scans
stderr for a traceback, both of which would be NEW assertions about the product. Site 2's
healthy offline pass really exits **1** (measured), so `assert_child_ran_clean` would have
failed a healthy run. Instead `tests/_child_diag.py` gained a narrow sibling,
`assert_child_was_not_signal_killed`, which delegates its whole message to
`child_failure_detail`. The AC's intent — do not re-derive the wording, every tier fails
identically — is met exactly; the letter naming `assert_child_ran_clean` is not, on purpose.

### The mechanism argument that replaced the authority argument

The guard rejects only a NEGATIVE returncode. My first justification for accepting a positive
`128+N` was *"rejecting it would be a widening"* — an argument from authority, about what a bug
fix is permitted to do. A reviewer challenged whether a shell-spawned child could report only
`137`, so I measured each site's real spawn path instead of reasoning from the call signature:

```
site1  bash killed          rc=-9    output_empty=True
site1  grandchild killed    rc=-9    output_empty=True   (bash execs into it)
site3  bash killed          rc=-9    output_empty=True
site3  grandchild killed    rc=137   output_empty=False
site5  make killed          rc=-9    output_empty=True
site5  recipe child killed  rc=2     output_empty=False
site2  direct child killed  rc=-9    output_empty=True   (no grandchild)
site4  direct child killed  rc=-9    output_empty=True   (no grandchild)
```

**An empty capture and a positive returncode never co-occur here.** The fail-open needs an
empty capture; whatever survives to report a `128+N` writes a diagnostic first, so the oracle
still has real output to inspect. The guard is therefore *coextensive with the hazard*, not
merely permitted. That argument survives someone disagreeing about scope; the first did not.

### The invariant is executable, with teeth

That premise is asserted at the three sites whose child has grandchildren; the two direct
spawns are excluded, since there a negative code is CPython's documented behaviour and pinning
it would be testing the standard library. Teeth proven by seeding the world the premise says is
impossible — site 3's bash surviving its killed grandchild and swallowing the diagnostic,
positive `137` with an empty capture — which turns it RED with exactly its intended message.
**11 mutations seeded, 11 killed, 0 survivors**, across the fix side, the shared predicate, the
shared message, and the kill side.

### A log that says "passed" is indistinguishable from a log that says "passed" about different code

I reported a full green sweep and pushed on it. That log's mtime was **five hours older than
my change** — a leftover from another session; my own sweep never finished, so the second never
started. CI caught what any real sweep would have.

That is the same shape as the bug this ticket is about, and it happened **five times in this
session's own instruments**: a colorized `grep "^FAILED"` reporting zero failures
unconditionally; a truncated sweep log identical to a clean one; an orphaned subshell reported
as finished; a `pgrep -f "make test"` matching the monitor's own command line and waiting on
itself; and the stale log. Each was caught only by checking the instrument against a
known-positive case. The first would have shipped a change claiming a kill matrix I had never
measured.

> **If you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still see a presence.**

Generalised in story `sphinxian-agrarian-snake`: ask of any check — *can this produce its
passing result for any reason other than the condition it claims to verify?*

### The residual risk I predicted and mis-dispositioned

My own residual-risk note said the bare `from _child_diag import …` "resolves only because the
root `tests/conftest.py` puts `tests/` on `sys.path`", and I had already hit that exact
`ModuleNotFoundError` in a scratch probe. I dispositioned it *"matched the repo's existing
pattern"* without checking whether any consumer loads those modules outside that context. One
does: `test_fixture_env_repr_security.py` loads `tests.interfaces.facades.test_cli` as a
`pytest_plugins` entry in a nested run rooted outside `tests/`. That is what reddened patchset 1
across all four matrix cells. The note was right; the disposition was wrong. Fixed in patchset 2
with the explicit bootstrap the `0e1d` precedent already uses.

### Last word

The gate that reddened this fix was itself an instance of the bug being fixed:
`_optionality.yml`'s new step did not copy the if-present skew guard that `_build-and-test.yml`
documents — the same defect as `7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14`, the ticket this bug attributes site 1 to.
The bug and the gate blocking its repair, one layer apart. Filed as `anxious-resistant-urson`
and since fixed at the source by change 2002.
